status: PROVISIONAL -- the same status as public-labels.json: the founder's clinicians confirm this wording.
comment: Words ONLY the ward console shows, kept out of public-labels.json because that table must cover exactly the enums the public page receives (tests/compliance/public_labels.test.ts and tests/db/public_labels_enum.test.ts hold it to that). `zero_reason` is app.zero_reason (002) in its declared order, which tests/compliance/ward_console_render.test.ts asserts. `offering_choice` is the publish form's choice between the two values of app.ward_offering: a ward CHOOSING what it offers, which is not the public line's statement of it. Moved here from the ward console's own code by R-2026-09-23-70 E, so the console holds no word table of its own. `session` holds the stop a session with NO ward is shown (R-2026-09-24-88 BP-8, wording accepted by R-2026-09-24-91 BS-2): zero rows from my_reporting_wards is never a legitimate ward, because a WARD_STAFF account always has its ward. It is an operator's session that fell back to this console, or broken data. The console appends its own support sentence, which names the support address (BR-2). `proxy` holds words the api.openbed.ng Worker itself writes, not the console: `VERIFY_LIMITED` is the one sentence a nurse reads when too many sign-in links were opened from one network in one 10-second window (R-2026-09-30-177 FA-3 e). supabase-proxy/handler.ts holds a copy, because that directory is outside the npm workspaces, and tests/compliance/proxy_limits_config.test.ts holds the two equal. Nothing in the console imports it.

session.NO_WARD: This sign-in isn't linked to a ward, so there is nothing to hand over. If you run OpenBed, sign in at admin.openbed.ng instead.

proxy.VERIFY_LIMITED: Too many sign-in links were opened from this network just now. Wait one minute, then open the same link again. It has not been used.
